note: A screen, not an audit: questions worth asking and the data needed to answer them. No savings are computed; typical benefits are the cited sources' general wording.

questions.question: Is this pump throttled by a control valve when it could run on a variable speed drive?

evidence.text: equipment P-1 reads "P-1 Recirculation pump"
valve LV-102 reads "LV-102 Discharge control valve to the alternate fuel tank" at RT-1

evidence.role: other control valve on the discharge
evidence.text: valve TV-104A reads "TV-104A Recirculation valve, heater leg" at E-2

evidence.role: other control valve on the discharge
evidence.text: valve TV-104B reads "TV-104B Recirculation valve, cooler leg" at E-3
instrument FT-103 reads "FT-103 Recirculation flow" at P-1
no speed control (SC, SIC, SY tag, VFD or VSD) on or next to the pump

data_requests.item: Control valve position (% open) over normal operation
where: historian or DCS trend for LV-102 (no historian tag is mapped in this model for these)
DCS/PLC configuration: the valve's controller output
a walkdown: read the positioner stroke indicator at several rates
data_requests.how: Take a month or more of valve output at normal sampling; note the typical and the lowest % open, and the hours at each.

data_requests.item: Flow over the same period (a flow-duration curve)
where: historian / recorded data: FT-103: digitized series 'recirc_flow_klbh' (from the source report's Fig 11)
site records: production rate records
data_requests.how: Bin the flow into ranges and count the hours in each.

where: the vendor datasheet: pump curve and rated duty point
the pump nameplate on P-1
data_requests.how: Copy the stated rated flow/head and units. These scalar fields do not establish a matching performance curve or actual operating duty.

where: the motor nameplate on P-1
maintenance records: motor record card
data_requests.how: Copy stated rated output and speed in their original units. Efficiency, identity and drive basis are separate review tasks.

where: a walkdown: elevations and pressures at the suction source and the delivery point
site records: line list or isometrics for pipe lengths and sizes
data_requests.how: Static head = lift plus pressure difference between source and destination; the rest of the pump head at duty is friction plus the valve drop.

data_requests.item: Matched pump curve, rated duty and system operating points
where: the vendor datasheet: pump curve and rated duty point
the pump nameplate on P-1
data_requests.how: Retain supplied ratings as unverified candidates. Review the curve against pump identity, installed impeller, speed, fluid, axes/units and revision; distinguish rated duty, BEP and actual operating points. A rating, URI or readability flag does not establish a matching curve or system suitability.

data_requests.item: Motor nameplate, efficiency and drive basis
where: the motor nameplate on P-1
maintenance records: motor record card
data_requests.how: Review existing nameplate or motor records for identity, rated shaft output in original units, speed, full-load efficiency and drive/bypass basis. HP/RPM alone do not establish efficiency or measured electrical input; retain missing or ambiguous evidence.

questions.decision_rule: Worth a drive quote when the valve normally runs well throttled for long hours and most of the head is friction rather than static lift (VSDs suit friction-dominated systems best). Close it if the valve normally runs near fully open, the head is mostly static, or the pump runs few hours.

typical_benefit.wording: "With rotodynamic pump installations, savings of between 30% and 50% have been achieved in many installations by installing VSDs." Also: "It is estimated that 75% of pump systems are oversized, many by more than 20%."
typical_benefit.arc: 2.4146 (IAC/ITAC browse page: 5,227 recommendations, 3.0 yr average payback, 31.4% implemented; average dollar figure omitted)

On an extracted drawing the links have no direction, so the rule takes a control valve within four drawn links that do not pass through other equipment; it may still be on a branch or the suction side, so check the drawing. questions.question: Is this hot line insulated?

evidence.text: stream S1 (asset stream:S1) reads "Flasher bottoms feed (methomyl-solvent liquid)"
no insulation code recorded for the line
Stated line/process temperature: S1 normal_temperature_C = 80
Supplied candidate fact, basis unverified: S1 normal_temperature_C = 80

data_requests.item: Insulation condition and length of bare pipe
where: site records: approved existing line list, insulation survey and inspection records
data_requests.how: Retain the identified line/location, survey date/revision, condition, length and pipe-size basis. Missing insulation metadata does not establish a bare line. Record unavailable or unsuitable evidence; new observations require the receiving organization's approved process.

where: site records: approved existing surface/insulation records or suitable documented analysis for this line
data_requests.how: Review line identity/location, source revision/date, surface versus fluid/design meaning, geometry and operating/ambient/time basis. Retain unreadable, wrong-asset, Boolean and unknown candidates without treating them as applicable evidence. Identify deliberate cooling or process constraints; no new live inspection, insulation installation or saving is established.

questions.decision_rule: Refer for engineering investigation when applicable evidence shows bare or damaged insulation on a hot line and no deliberate cooling or process constraint rules it out. The cited surface-temperature criterion is a source screening reference, not an automatic site instruction. Close only the bounded investigation when reviewed evidence settles its scope; this screen does not authorize insulation work.

typical_benefit.wording: "Insulation can typically reduce energy losses by 90%." "Any surface over 120°F should be insulated." LBNL (as reported in LBNL-56183): insulation 3-13%, 1.1 yr.

questions.question: Is heat rejected to cooling water in one place while steam heats a colder stream in another (a heat-integration question)?

evidence.text: stream U2 (asset stream:U2) reads "Cooling water (80 C) supply to the cooler" at E-3
hand valve HV-112 reads "HV-112 Cooling water supply valve" at E-3
stream U1 (asset stream:U1) reads "Steam supply to the heater" at E-2
instrument FT-106 reads "FT-106 Indicated steam flow to the heater" at E-2
valve TV-104C reads "TV-104C Steam flow valve to the heater (Fig 10: Temperature Control Valve)" at E-2
hand valve HV-108 reads "HV-108 Steam block valve, heater steam supply" at E-2

data_requests.item: Temperatures and duties of the cooled and the heated streams
where: only a valve (HV-112) is drawn on this line, with no flow measurement; flow needs a meter or a calibrated valve curve
historian or DCS trend for FT-106 (no historian tag is mapped in this model for these)
site records: heat and material balance
data_requests.how: For each stream: supply and target temperature and duty.

data_requests.item: Whether the duties overlap in time
where: site records: operating sequence: are both duties needed at the same time?
data_requests.how: Mark each duty continuous, batch or startup-only.

where: a walkdown: distance between the two exchangers
maintenance records: cleaning history
data_requests.how: Note pipe run and fouling service.

questions.decision_rule: Worth a pinch or exchanger study only when the hot stream's temperature range sits above the cold stream's with a practical approach, both run at the same time for long hours, and they are close enough to connect. Otherwise close it.

questions.question: Is high-grade (or unknown-grade) steam doing a low-temperature job?

evidence.text: stream U1 (asset stream:U1) reads "Steam supply to the heater" at E-2
valve TV-104C reads "TV-104C Steam flow valve to the heater (Fig 10: Temperature Control Valve)" at E-2

controller TIC-104 reads "TIC-104 Split-range temperature control: heats through the heater (steam valve and heater-leg valve) during startup; at the setpoint it closes the steam valve and moves recirculation from the heater to the cooler (setpoint 135 C)" As found: incorrectly programmed: changing from heating to cooling closed the recirculation valves to both the heater and the cooler, blocking all recirculation flow (p. 39, footnote 29; CSB: not causal).
equipment E-2 reads "E-2 Recirculation heater (steam)"

where: site records: approved supply/header list and existing pressure/temperature records
data_requests.how: Retain the stated pressure/temperature fields and exact source basis. Their presence does not establish representative actual supply conditions; pressure reference, steam state and operating applicability remain separate review tasks.

where: DCS/PLC configuration: the temperature setpoint
data_requests.how: Note setpoint and normal range.

data_requests.item: A lower-grade heat source on site (a lower steam header, exhaust or waste heat) with spare capacity
where: site records: site steam balance
a walkdown: headers and hot streams near this user
data_requests.how: List sources whose temperature exceeds the need with a practical approach.

data_requests.item: Applicable steam-supply conditions and operating basis
where: site records: approved existing supply/user configuration and coincident operating-condition records
data_requests.how: Review supply/user identity and location, source revision, pressure units and gauge/absolute reference, steam condition, coincident period/mode and design-versus-actual basis. Unknown, Boolean, wrong-asset or noncoincident candidates remain unresolved. Saturation temperature is only a conditional reference after the pressure basis/state are established; never infer actual superheated temperature from pressure alone. No new live measurement or change is instructed.

questions.decision_rule: Worth a change only if a lower-grade source can meet the needed temperature with margin, for the hours the user runs; if the steam is already the lowest grade available, close it.

typical_benefit.wording: Closest source wordings: pinch potential "far exceeds that from well-known conventional techniques such as heat recovery from boiler flue gas, insulation and steam trap management" (S19, no % stated); for letdown to the lower pressure, S6's turbogenerator condition. No source gives a number for matching steam grade to duty.
source_titles: S19: Worrell & Galitsky, Energy Efficiency Improvement and Cost Saving Opportunities for Petroleum Refineries: An ENERGY STAR Guide (LBNL-56183, Feb 2005)
S6: Steam Tip #20, Replace Pressure-Reducing Valves with Backpressure Turbogenerators (DOE/GO-102012-3409)

questions.limits: Where the model does not state the steam grade, first identify its source and applicable conditions. Design limits and generic named fields do not establish coincident operation, current user demand or an available alternative source. Supplied candidates need explicit suitability review; no default state, pressure conversion or change recommendation is inferred.

questions.question: Is heat rejected to cooling water at a temperature another user could use?

hand valve HV-112 reads "HV-112 Cooling water supply valve" at E-3
Cooling water supply temperature: E-3 cooling_water_C = 80

where: a walkdown: thermometer on the return
data_requests.how: Record at normal operation; the return temperature is the grade of the heat on offer.

data_requests.item: Temperature of the stream being cooled (in and out)
where: site records: heat and material balance
data_requests.how: Record at normal operation.

where: the vendor datasheet: exchanger datasheet
site records: heat and material balance
data_requests.how: Review exchanger identity, units and rated-versus-actual basis. A generic CAPACITY may denote flow or design capacity, not heat duty. Retain coincident flow, heat-capacity basis and inlet/return temperatures over a stated period, or a documented heat balance; supplied scalars do not establish usable recovered heat.

data_requests.item: A heat user that needs heat below the return temperature
where: site records: list of heating duties with temperatures
a walkdown: users nearby
data_requests.how: Match by temperature, hours and distance.

questions.decision_rule: Worth a study only if the heat leaves hotter than a nearby user needs, for overlapping hours; cooling water returning only a few degrees above ambient closes it.

typical_benefit.wording: Closest source wording (S19, pinch): potential "far exceeds that from well-known conventional techniques such as heat recovery from boiler flue gas, insulation and steam trap management." No % stated. For air compressors S11 says recovery "anywhere from 50 to 90 percent" of the heat, which applies to compressors only.
source_titles: S19: Worrell & Galitsky, Energy Efficiency Improvement and Cost Saving Opportunities for Petroleum Refineries: An ENERGY STAR Guide (LBNL-56183, Feb 2005)

questions.question: What source-labelled trip or interlock records apply to each rotating or fired machine, and what remains unverified?

evidence.text: equipment P-1 reads "P-1 Recirculation pump"
interlock IL-1 reads "IL-1 TT-104 below the minimum temperature setpoint FV-107 held closed"
interlock IL-2 reads "IL-2 PT-101 at or above the maximum pressure setpoint FV-107 held closed"
interlock IL-3 reads "IL-3 FT-103 recirculation flow not established FV-107 held closed"

where: site records: cause-and-effect matrix, HAZOP and LOPA reports
DCS/PLC configuration: safety system configuration
data_requests.how: Review existing cause-and-effect, governing requirements and configuration records for each named machine, with their revisions and applicability. Retain supplied trip/switch indications as candidates; a drawing label or an unrelated function does not settle the records or establish effective, tested protection. Missing model information is not evidence that installed protection is absent.

where: site records: source-labelled function identifiers, initiating measurements, final elements and protected-machine targets, shared scope and revisions; governing requirements and validation/test evidence where applicable
DCS/PLC configuration: existing configuration and its documented measurement/action/final-element identities, read through the approved site process
data_requests.how: Keep each machine in the review even where a switch or trip is supplied. Retain all explicit shared targets and supplied qualifiers; unknown or contradictory targets remain unresolved. Same-model text or nearby equipment does not prove function coverage. Record a responsible person or authority separately from protected-machine association; neither is inferred here. This requests record review, not a new test, safety design or operating action.

questions.decision_rule: A qualified site review may resolve the source-labelled machine/function associations and remaining record requests using applicable current evidence. A supplied trip, switch, cause/effect row or shared-function label alone establishes neither complete coverage nor installed protection adequacy. This screen grants no acceptance or authority and performs no safety validation.

typical_benefit.wording: Safety benefit; no energy source. Present it as a question to verify, not a finding.

questions.limits: P&IDs often leave trips to separate cause-and-effect records. Missing or unknown model evidence does not establish missing installed protection. Supplied associations, shared targets, revisions and contradictions require review; no machine, person owner, approval, tested condition or effective protection is inferred. C9 has no primary safety-design source cited in the catalog and remains a question for record review, not safety design, SIL assignment, a legal-compliance assessment or an operating recommendation.
